sections.text: A **ratio** compares two amounts. 2 red marbles to 3 blue marbles is **2:3**, "2 to 3", or ⅔. A bar cut into 5 parts with 2 shaded shows the red part out of the whole.
**Order matters!** "Red to blue" is 2:3, but "blue to red" is 3:2.
Ratios can compare **part to part** (2:3) or **part to whole** (2:5, since 2 + 3 = 5). For 4 guards and 6 forwards, guards to all players is 4:10.

learn.keyIdea: Ratio a:b compares a to b — say it in the same order as the words.

examples.title: Part to part
examples.prompt: A team has 4 guards and 6 forwards. What is the ratio of guards to forwards in simplest form?

steps.why: The words say guards, then forwards.

steps.do: Divide both by 2: 2:3, which is 5 parts in all (2 + 3 = 5).
steps.why: Dividing both parts by the same number keeps the same comparison.

examples.mistake: 6:4 is forwards to guards — the order is backwards.

examples.title: Part to whole
examples.prompt: Same team (4 guards, 6 forwards): what is the ratio of guards to all players?
examples.check: 2 of every 5 players are guards, and 4 of 10 matches. ✅
examples.mistake: Don't use 4:6 — that compares guards to forwards, not to everyone.

examples.title: Sharing by a ratio
examples.prompt: Boys to girls is 2:3 in a class of 25 students. How many boys are there?

steps.why: Count how many groups fit in the class.

examples.mistake: Don't just divide 25 by 2 — the ratio is out of 5, not 2.

guided.prompt: There are 7 cats and 4 dogs. What is the ratio of dogs to cats?

steps.why: Dogs are named first, so they go first.
steps.hint: Read the order in the question.

guided.prompt: Write 12:18 in simplest form.

steps.do: What is the GCF of 12 and 18?
steps.why: Dividing by the GCF gives simplest form.
steps.hint: Both are in the 6 times table.

guided.prompt: A bag has 3 red and 5 blue marbles. What fraction of all the marbles are red?

steps.do: How many marbles are there in all?
steps.why: Part to whole needs the total.

steps.do: Write red out of all as a fraction.
steps.why: Red is the part and 8 is the whole.
steps.worked: ⅜ of the marbles are red.

guided.prompt: Boys to girls is 3:4. There are 28 students. How many girls are there?

steps.do: How many students are in each 3 + 4 group?

steps.why: Divide the total by the group size.

sections.text: A **unit rate** tells how much for **one**: miles *per* hour, dollars *per* item. 150 miles in 3 hours means 50 miles each hour: 50, 100, 150.
Find it by dividing: 150 ÷ 3 = **50 miles per hour**.
Unit rates work with fractions too. ½ cup oats for ¼ cup milk: two ¼s fit in ½, so there are 2 cups of oats per cup of milk.

learn.keyIdea: Unit rate = first amount ÷ second amount (how much per 1).

examples.title: Price per item
examples.prompt: $18 for 6 pens. What is the cost per pen?

steps.do: Divide the cost by the number of pens: 18 ÷ 6.

steps.why: Each of the 6 pens gets an equal share.

examples.mistake: 6 ÷ 18 gives pens per dollar, not dollars per pen.

examples.title: Speed of typing
examples.prompt: 225 words in 5 minutes. How many words per minute?

steps.why: Each minute gets an equal share of words.

examples.mistake: Make sure the 'per' quantity is the one you divide by.

examples.title: Fraction unit rate
examples.prompt: ½ cup oats for every ¼ cup milk. How many cups of oats per cup of milk?

steps.why: We want the amount of oats for 1 whole cup of milk.
Keep, change, flip turns division into multiplication.

examples.mistake: ½ × ¼ = ⅛ multiplies instead of dividing.

guided.prompt: 5 apples cost $10. What is the cost of 1 apple in dollars?
A car travels 180 miles in 4 hours. How many miles per hour is that?

steps.why: Miles per hour means miles for 1 hour.

guided.prompt: A runner goes 3 miles in ½ hour. How many miles per hour is that?

steps.do: What is the reciprocal of ½?
steps.why: Dividing by ½ is multiplying by its flip.
This gives the miles for 1 whole hour.

guided.prompt: ¾ cup sugar for every ½ cup flour. How many cups of sugar per cup of flour?

steps.do: Divide ¾ ÷ ½. Type the answer as a fraction.
steps.why: Per cup of flour means divide by the flour amount.

sections.text:
In a **ratio table**, every row is an **equivalent ratio**. Multiply both numbers by the same amount.

| Blue | Yellow |
|---|---|
| 2 | 3 |
| 4 | 6 |
| 6 | 9 |
Plot the rows as points (2, 3), (4, 6), (6, 9). Equivalent ratios make a straight line through (0, 0)!
To fill a missing value, find what you multiplied by. 3:4 = ?:20: 4 × 5 = 20, so 3 × 5 = 15.

learn.keyIdea: Multiply or divide both parts by the same number.

examples.title: Missing value

steps.why: Find how the known parts are related.
The other part must be multiplied by the same 5.

examples.mistake: Adding 16 to both parts (19:20) doesn't keep the ratio.

examples.title: Using a unit rate
examples.prompt: 4 muffins use 6 eggs. How many eggs for 10 muffins?

steps.why: Finding the amount for 1 muffin makes any amount easy.
Each of the 10 muffins needs 1.5 eggs.

examples.mistake: 10 + 2 = 12 adds instead of scaling.

examples.title: Is it equivalent?
examples.prompt: Is (8, 12) equivalent to the ratio 2:3?

steps.why: Check if one factor works for both parts.

steps.do: Both use 4, so yes: (2, 3) and (8, 12) line up.
steps.why: Equivalent ratios scale both parts the same.

examples.mistake: (8, 13) would not work — the factors must match exactly.

guided.prompt: Complete: 2:5 = ?:30

steps.do: What do you multiply 5 by to get 30?

steps.why: Both parts use the same factor.

guided.prompt: A recipe uses 3 cups flour for 2 cups milk. How many cups of flour for 8 cups milk?

steps.do: What do you multiply 2 by to get 8?

steps.why: Flour scales by the same factor.
steps.worked: 12 cups flour. The points (2, 3) and (8, 12) are on the same line.

guided.prompt: Paint is 4 cups blue to 7 cups yellow. Which pair (blue, yellow) makes the same color?

steps.why: Equivalent ratios multiply both parts by the same number.

guided.prompt: 6 lemons make 9 cups of lemonade. How many lemons for 15 cups?

steps.do: Unit rate: how many lemons per cup? Type as a fraction.
steps.why: Lemons for 1 cup helps scale to any amount.

sections.text: The **unit price** is the price for one unit: price ÷ quantity. A 4-pack of yogurt for $3.00 costs 3.00 ÷ 4 = $0.75 each.
To compare deals, find each unit price. **Lowest unit price = best buy!** 12 oz for $3.60 is $0.30 per oz; 16 oz for $4.00 is $0.25 per oz.
Once you know the unit price, multiply to price any amount. 💰

learn.keyIdea: Unit price = price ÷ quantity; lowest unit price wins.

examples.title: Price for one
examples.prompt: A 4-pack of yogurt costs $3.00. What is the price per yogurt?
examples.mistake: 4 ÷ 3.00 gives yogurts per dollar instead.

examples.title: Best buy
examples.prompt: A smaller size is 12 oz for $3.60 and a bigger size is 16 oz for $4.00. Which size is the better buy?

steps.why: Unit prices put both deals on the same scale.

steps.do: 0.25 < 0.30, so the 16 oz size is the better buy.
steps.why: Lower price per ounce saves money.

examples.check: 16 oz at $0.30 would cost $4.80, more than $4.00. ✅
examples.mistake: The cheaper total price isn't always the better buy.

examples.title: Scaling up
examples.prompt: 3 tickets cost $22.50. What do 8 tickets cost?

steps.why: Find the price of 1 ticket first.
Multiply the unit price by the number of tickets.

examples.mistake: Don't multiply 22.50 × 8 — that's the price of 24 tickets.

guided.prompt: 6 granola bars cost $3.00. What is the price of 1 bar in dollars?
A 5-pack of pens costs $4.25. What is the price per pen in dollars?

steps.why: Each pen gets an equal share.

guided.prompt: Brand A: 10 oz for $2.50. Brand B: 16 oz for $3.20. Which is the better buy?

steps.do: Brand A price per oz in dollars?
Brand B price per oz in dollars?
steps.why: Same units for a fair comparison.

guided.prompt: 4 notebooks cost $7.00. How many dollars do 10 notebooks cost?

steps.do: Find the price of 1 notebook in dollars.
steps.why: The unit price helps you scale.

sections.text: **speed = distance ÷ time.** 120 miles in 2 hours is 60 miles each hour.
**distance = speed × time.** At 45 mph for 3 hours: 45, 90, 135 miles.
**time = distance ÷ speed.** Constant speed means the same distance every hour. 🚴

learn.keyIdea: d = s × t (cover one to find it!).

examples.title: Find speed
examples.prompt: 120 miles in 2 hours. What is the speed in miles per hour?

steps.why: Each hour covers the same 60 miles.

examples.mistake: 2 ÷ 120 is hours per mile, not miles per hour.

examples.title: Find distance
examples.prompt: At 45 mph, how far do you go in 3 hours?
examples.mistake: Don't divide 45 by 3 — more hours means more distance.

examples.title: Find time
examples.prompt: At 8 km per hour, how long to go 20 km?

steps.why: Count how many 8-km hours fit in 20 km.

steps.do: 20 ÷ 8 = 2.5 hours: 8 km, 16 km, then 4 more km in half an hour.
steps.why: Two full hours make 16 km, and half an hour makes 4 more.

examples.mistake: Don't multiply 20 × 8 — that's not a time.

guided.prompt: A cyclist rides 36 miles in 3 hours. What is the speed in miles per hour?
A train goes 70 miles per hour. How many miles does it go in 4 hours?
At 50 miles per hour, how many hours to go 175 miles?

steps.do: How many full hours fit (50 × ? ≤ 175)? Remember 50 × 3 = 150.
Divide 175 ÷ 50 for the exact time in hours.
steps.why: The leftover 25 miles is half an hour.

guided.prompt: Andrew walks 2 miles in 40 minutes at a steady pace. How many miles does he walk in 1 hour?

steps.do: How many 20-minute blocks are in 40 minutes?
steps.why: Breaking time into blocks helps find the rate.

steps.do: 1 hour = 3 blocks of 20 minutes. Miles in 1 hour?

sections.text: **Percent** means *per hundred*. 35% is 35 out of 100 squares on a 10-by-10 grid: 7 rows of 5 is 35.
To find a percent of a number, multiply. 30% of 80 = 30/100 × 80 = **24**. On a number line from 0 to 80, 30% lands at 24.
To find the whole: if 15 is 25%, then 100% is 4 times as much: **60**.

learn.keyIdea: Percent = out of 100: part = percent/100 × whole.

examples.title: Percent of a number
examples.prompt: What is 30% of 80?

steps.why: Finding a part of a number means multiplying.

examples.title: Fraction to percent
examples.prompt: Write ⅗ as a percent.

steps.do: Make the bottom 100: multiply top and bottom by 20.

examples.mistake: ⅗ is not 35% — don't just write the digits next to each other.

examples.title: Find the whole
examples.prompt: 15 is 25% of what number?
examples.mistake: 25% of 15 (3.75) answers a different question.

guided.prompt: What is 50% of 64?
Write 7/20 as a percent (just the number).

steps.do: What do you multiply 20 by to get 100?

steps.why: Top and bottom both get multiplied by 5.

guided.prompt: A $60 game is 15% off. How many dollars do you save?
18 is 30% of what number?

sections.text: Use a conversion ratio like **1 foot = 12 inches**. 5 feet is 5 jumps of 12: 12, 24, 36, 48, 60 inches.
Big unit → small unit: **multiply**. Small unit → big unit: **divide**. 240 seconds ÷ 60 = 4 minutes.
1 meter = 100 centimeters, so 350 cm = 3.5 m. On 4 meter-bars cut in halves, 7 halves are shaded: three full meters and half of another.

learn.keyIdea: Big → small: multiply. Small → big: divide.

examples.title: Feet to inches
examples.prompt: How many inches are in 5 feet?

steps.why: Big unit to small unit means more of them, so multiply.

examples.mistake: Dividing 5 ÷ 12 gives a tiny number — inches should be more than feet.

examples.title: Seconds to minutes
examples.prompt: Convert 240 seconds to minutes.

steps.why: Small unit to big unit means fewer, so divide.

examples.mistake: 240 × 60 makes the number bigger — minutes should be fewer.

examples.title: Centimeters to meters
examples.prompt: Convert 350 centimeters to meters.

steps.why: Dividing by 100 moves the decimal point 2 places left.

examples.mistake: 35 m would be 3,500 cm — move the decimal 2 places, not 1.

guided.prompt: How many inches are in 3 feet?
Convert 8 quarts to gallons. (1 gallon = 4 quarts)

steps.why: Small unit to big unit, so divide.

guided.prompt: How many ounces are in 2.5 pounds? (1 pound = 16 ounces)

steps.do: Total ounces? (On 3 pound-bars cut in halves, 5 halves make 2.5 pounds.)

guided.prompt: A 1.2 km trail: how many meters long is it? (1 km = 1000 m)

steps.why: Big unit to small unit, so multiply.

Write the ratio 66:72 in simplest form.
questions.explanation: Divide both parts by their GCF, 6: 66 ÷ 6 = 11, 72 ÷ 6 = 12. So 11:12.

questions.explanation: Each group of 9+2 = 11 students has 2 girls. 66 ÷ 11 = 6 groups, so 6 × 2 = 12 girls.

questions.prompt: Write the ratio 9:15 in simplest form.

questions.prompt: There are 2 red marbles and 3 blue marbles. What is the ratio of red marbles to blue marbles?

questions.prompt: Write the ratio 39:18 in simplest form.

questions.prompt: Write the ratio 18:60 in simplest form.
questions.explanation: Divide both parts by their GCF, 6: 18 ÷ 6 = 3, 60 ÷ 6 = 10. So 3:10.

Write the ratio 48:28 in simplest form.
questions.explanation: Divide both parts by their GCF, 4: 48 ÷ 4 = 12, 28 ÷ 4 = 7. So 12:7.

questions.prompt: In Andrew's class, the ratio of boys to girls is 2:5. There are 35 students. How many girls are there?

Write the ratio 48:44 in simplest form.
questions.explanation: Divide both parts by their GCF, 4: 48 ÷ 4 = 12, 44 ÷ 4 = 11. So 12:11.
